<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Project maintenance instructions

## Current organization — 20 October 2026

The user explicitly requested experiment-owned folders, superseding the historical root-level data/reports/notebooks arrangement. Read [README.md](README.md), [experiments/README.md](experiments/README.md), and [maintenance/README.md](maintenance/README.md).

- Each experiment owns `hypotheses/`, `prompts/`, `data/`, `analysis/`, `reports/`, and `notebooks/`. Shared source, scripts and tests remain outside under `src/`, `scripts/` and `tests/`.
- Current new work belongs in `experiments/13_weekly_state_api_20261021/` and its separately versioned implementation. Experiment 12 is preserved as the completed whole-cohort feasibility collection. Do not mix the samples.
- The user explicitly authorized weekly batches on 21 October 2026, superseding the earlier one-response requirement: 80 fictional testers in 20 four-role chains per model, 24 Python-calculated decision weeks. All 80 orders for a week share one response; treat identities as dependent. This does not establish independent student-level significance.
- Preserve every historical file's exact current bytes. The move map and hashes are `maintenance/reorganization_20261020/FILE_MAP.json`. A scientific change needs a new protocol/fingerprint; do not edit frozen source, prompts, manifests, responses or original publications to fit new results.
- Old reports and notebooks may contain original paths. Use the new experiment guides for navigation and `scripts/legacy_workspace.py` for saved-data replay in a disposable old-layout copy. Do not monkeypatch frozen code or rewrite recorded Windows source paths.
- Historical paid entry points depend on the original `data/runs` location for cumulative spending. They must not be used directly from this reorganized root. A new API study needs explicit cumulative accounting and a hard total cap including pilots and failed requests. Never rename campaigns to bypass prior spending.
- The user authorized four-model API testing with a cumulative $5 cap and explicitly carried that SAME cap into experiment 13. Experiment 12 data/api_budget.json remains the shared ledger and lock owner. Preserve its existing $0.3404859 in recorded charges; this is not a fresh $5. Any future budget increase requires explicit authorization. Keys are supplied only by the user in hidden notebook fields.
- Credentials remain in environment variables or hidden prompts, never files, notebook outputs, command arguments, logs or reports.
- Do not force interior/positive orders, supply a preferred maximum, encode the desired hypothesis direction, tune for significance, or fabricate missing decisions. Preserve null/opposite outcomes and failed attempts. Software controls must be labeled synthetic.
- Preserve actual provider/model labels and requested/reported settings separately. Prompted pressure is a fictional framing treatment unless computation or time is actually restricted and measured.
- Update the experiment's own README with changes, run instructions, validation and limitations. New reports put short numbered conclusions first. Run checks proportionate to changes.

The original complete instruction history is preserved in [original_navigation/AGENTS.md](maintenance/reorganization_20261020/original_navigation/AGENTS.md). Its frozen-study preservation requirements remain relevant; its old folder paths are resolved through the move map.

## Existing integrity issue

Before reorganization, 14,435 of the saved 15,013-file baseline had LF bytes where its hashes expected CRLF; 578 already matched. All mismatches were line-ending-only. Do not claim the canonical checkout matches the historical byte baseline. The compatibility helper recovers historical bytes only in a temporary copy and only when an existing expected hash proves the conversion. Keep its derivation receipt separate from migration verification.

The latest received Astra study is complete at 6/6. Its unchanged prepared GPT-6 / Pro parent remains 0/6 for provenance; it is not an outstanding request. No extra responses belong in that closed sample. See experiment 11 for reports and intake records.

You simulate hypothetical second-year business students at the University at Buffalo, an American university. They are fictional participants, not actual students. Keep their supplied ordinary-coursework profiles consistent. Make plausible student decisions based on the current displayed information and that group's classroom reading. Their aim is to minimize cumulative team inventory-holding and backlog costs in a continuing game. Do not invent differences between students or groups to satisfy an experiment.

There are three groups, each containing 50 four-role chains. The helper selects their sequence. Complete all three groups in this chat. Each group has 24 decision weeks followed by separate hypothetical order decisions. The groups share this chat's context; do not claim they are independent experiments.

Rules: roles are retailer, wholesaler, distributor, factory. Each order is a nonnegative integer. Holding costs 0.5 per case/week; backlog costs 1 per case/week. Backlog already includes current unfilled demand. Outstanding replenishment is previously ordered goods not yet received. Upstream order information takes one week; shipments take two weeks; factory production takes three weeks. Orders cannot be cancelled. Python handles receipts and shipments before decisions. All displayed inventories are shared. Future demand is unknown. Treat the game as continuing beyond the scored horizon; do not liquidate stock just because the export ends.

SETUP 鈥?run this once in Python. Change only the ZIP path to its actual uploaded location. Do not display helper source, inspect private state/RNG, read other project files, or change the helper. Reading the named ZIP entries as bytes to install them is allowed; printing or examining their source is not.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json, sys, tempfile, zipfile

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='beer_game_'))
with zipfile.ZipFile(uploaded_zip) as z:
    for name in ('beergame_controller.py', 'batch_runner.py'):
        (work / name).write_bytes(z.read(name))
sys.path.insert(0, str(work))
from batch_runner import Batch
run = Batch(model_slot='gpt_luna')
print(json.dumps(run.display(), separators=(',', ':')))
run.save(work)
```

Hypothetical `probes` are arrays described by `probe_columns`. The shared-inventory array always follows the four-role order.
- For `initial` or `revision`, choose 100 literal integer orders for the CURRENT PAGE: a dictionary mapping exactly its 25 `requested_ids` to [retailer, wholesaler, distributor, factory]. - Call `run.submit(YOUR_LITERAL_DICTIONARY)` and print its returned display. Then call `run.save(work)` to checkpoint. Replace the placeholder with actual literal choices; do not run a placeholder. Each next decision must follow a newly returned tool display.
- A `revision` / `probe_revision` phase requires a SEPARATE assistant/tool interaction after seeing initial proposals. You may keep or change any order. Other phases commit initial choices. Do not combine initial and revision submissions in one tool call.
- A group has 50 chains: each weekly opportunity has two pages, and each probe opportunity has eight pages. Submit every page in sequence. The helper commits the entire opportunity only after all its pages are supplied, then begins revision or advances the game as appropriate. Do not interpret a new page as a new week. Later pages must not retroactively change earlier submitted choices.
- Continue until the returned top-level phase is `complete`. The next group starts automatically. Do not stop after the first group or after the game weeks before completing probes. Show only brief progress updates (group, week, page), without analyzing comparisons.

DECISIONS MUST COME FROM YOU
Python is for physical accounting, storage and formatting only. Do not write a policy, optimizer, random-order generator, decision loop, or formula that supplies orders. Do not precompute future choices, copy an earlier group's decisions, or run multiple submissions in one tool call. Choose the literal orders after each current display. Do not calculate p-values, compare groups, or search for a desired result during collection. Do not provide hidden reasoning traces; the visible choices and tool calls are the required record.

RETURN ONE FILE

Provide a downloadable link to that exact JSON. It contains all three groups, weekly orders, probes and controller records. Do not replace it with a summary or edited table.
